rounds.proof_sketch: block_size=256 → 8 warps → warp_id ∈ {0..7} → max index accessed = 7 < 31. Both array sizes (31 and 32) accommodate indices 0-7. Access pattern determined by block_size, not input values.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation reduces the shared memory array from 32 to 31 elements. With the fixed block_size of 256 threads, there are exactly 8 warps per block (256/32=8). The warp_id ranges from 0 to 7, meaning only indices 0-7 are ever written to or read from the warp_maxs array. Since 31 > 8, the reduced array size is still sufficient to hold all warp maxima. No input values can change the thread/warp structure - this is determined solely by the compile-time constant block_size=256.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under fixed configuration. The mutation would only be observable if block_size exceeded 992 (requiring 31+ warps), but block_size=256 is hardcoded. No value-level input can affect shared memory indexing patterns.
rounds.recommendations: For mutation testing of shared memory array sizes, test coverage should verify that the array bounds are actually exercised by the thread/block configuration. In this case, the mutation tool generated a semantically equivalent mutant because the original array was oversized (32 slots for only 8 warps). Consider adding assertions or documenting the relationship between block_size and shared memory requirements.
